label: EdgeRouter X
description: EdgeRouter X (ER-X) - 5x 10/100/1000 RJ45: eth0 (port1) accepts 24V passive PoE, eth4 (port5) is a 24V passive PoE passthrough. 5 W max.

poe.note: The passthrough is a pass-through of the input supply, so Ubiquiti prints no fixed budget: the quick-start guide's table gives the available output per input source - "24V passive PoE (on eth0/PoE In) = approx. 23V, 5W", "12V, 1A (ERLite-3 Power Adapter) = approx. 11V, 5W", "24V, 2.5A (ERPoe-5 Power Adapter) = approx. 23V, 11W". 5 W is the vendor's own figure for the configuration the datasheet also names as a power method (24V passive PoE on eth0), not an arithmetic derivation. Ubiquiti's footnote "Requires 24V passive PoE or a 12W minimum power adapter" is a minimum *adapter* rating, not a per-port PoE ceiling - no page states a per-port ceiling for the ER-X (the datasheet's "Max. PoE Wattage Per Data/PoE Output Port 12W (24V)" row belongs to the ER-X-SFP table on the same page). A lab that fits a 24V/2.5A supply can declare 11 W.

notes: Ubiquiti sources read 2026-11-19: datasheet https://dl.ui.com/datasheets/edgemax/EdgeRouter_X_DS.pdf (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 3,594,850 B, 7 pages, "Models: ER-X, ER-X-SFP") and quick-start guide https://dl.ui.com/guides/edgemax/EdgeRouter_ER-X_QSG.pdf (200, application/pdf, 1,362,583 B, 18 pages). Networking interfaces, datasheet ER-X table: **Data/PoE Input Port (1) 10/100/1000 RJ45 Port; Data Ports (3) 10/100/1000 RJ45 Ports; Data/PoE Passthrough Port (1) 10/100/1000 RJ45 Port** - five copper ports, of which one sinks and one sources power. Power: **Max. Power Consumption 5W; Power Input 12VDC, 0.5A Power Adapter (Included) or 24V Passive PoE; Supported Voltage Range 9 to 26VDC**. QSG port names, which the catalogue keeps as port1-port5 in vendor order: **eth0/PoE In** (accepts 24V passive PoE), **eth1-eth3** (data only), **eth4/PoE Out** (passive passthrough). Trap recorded: the tech-spec page (https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/er-x, 200, 575,859 B) prints "Metworking interface: (3) 10/100/1000 RJ45 ports" - a typo, and only the *data* ports - because its next row, "PoE interface", carries "(1) ... (Data/PoE input)" and "(1) ... (Data/PoE passthrough)". Reading the 3 as the port count deletes the PoE pair; the datasheet's five-port table above is the authority. Second trap: no ER-X datasheet exists under the flat or legacy paths - dl.ui.com/datasheets/ER-X.pdf, dl.ui.com/qig/er-x/ and dl.ubnt.com/datasheets/edgerouterx/ER-X_DS.pdf all answer 200 with the 609,911-byte tech-specs front page, the silent fallback this thread has trapped before. The datasheets/edgemax/ path is the one that resolves. **Why `poeIn: false` and not `poe-pd` as a capability:** `isPoePd()` returns true for a whole device as soon as its capability list contains `poe-pd`, and `engine/media.js` then gives every silent copper port a 12.95 W draw - so the device-level token turned port2-port4 into phantom powered devices (15 W of draw the hardware cannot take). The one port that can sink power carries the figure itself.
